concerns.text: Recall (SC-006) cannot be estimated from the planned audit design. The stratified sample is drawn ONLY from detected findings (audit.py samples 'findings'), so false negatives (vulnerabilities the tools missed) are never observed. Precision and FPR are computable; recall is not. The plan must either sample non-flagged code regions/files as well, or explicitly re-scope SC-006 to precision-only.

concerns.location: plan.md: Phase 1 / spec FR-001; research.md Dataset Strategy
concerns.text: Construct validity of the comparison groups is unaddressed. The spec's suggested human-written corpus is the Juliet Test Suite — synthetic test cases deliberately constructed to contain vulnerabilities. Using Juliet as the 'human' group would confound the LLM-vs-human comparison almost entirely. The plan defers dataset selection but never states selection criteria (e.g., comparable task domains, languages, provenance) that would make the two groups construct-comparable. Add group-comparability criteria to the dataset amendment.

Language is an obvious confound (LLM corpora are often Python-heavy; human corpora Java-heavy) and tool coverage differs by language (Bandit is Python-only). The NB model includes only group as predictor with a log(LOC) offset. Add language as a covariate or pre-specify per-language / language-stratified analysis, and report group language composition.

concerns.location: plan.md: Phase 4, Task 6; research.md Statistical rigor notes
concerns.text: Power is acknowledged as a limitation but no minimum detectable effect or planned sensitivity analysis is stated. With deferred dataset sizes, specify at least: the n≥30 fallback decision rule applied per group per language, and that the NB dispersion parameter will be reported so readers can judge estimate stability.

MW-U on per-file densities and NB on counts are not independent tests of the same hypothesis (different response scales); BH correction across them is defensible but the plan should state the family definition (one hypothesis, two estimators) so the correction choice is not misread as testing two distinct claims.

FR-001 mandates downloading CodeVulnBench and a verified human-written subset 'from public repositories, ensuring all files are accessible and valid before analysis begins.' The plan (Summary; research.md Dataset Strategy) states NO verified public source exists for either dataset. The FR is unbacked by any verifiable plan element — the spec must be amended to name a verified open dataset pair (or the FR relaxed) before execution can satisfy it. The plan correctly surfaces this; the spec is the root cause.

FR-002 requires executing 'Bandit, Semgrep, SonarQube' on all samples. The plan (Phase 2, Task 3; Complexity Tracking) drops SonarQube entirely, citing runner constraints. This is a direct spec/plan contradiction: either the spec FR-002 and Constitution VI must be amended to a two-tool pipeline, or the plan must include a SonarQube execution path. As written, FR-002 has no fully satisfying plan element.

FR-008/SC-007 require FPR computed per group from human audit results. Plan Task 8 allows reporting 'not_available' if no auditor verdicts exist at run time. The spec's assumption 'Human auditors are available' is load-bearing for FR-008; the plan's fallback leaves FR-008 potentially unmeasured with no spec-level amendment. Spec should be amended to define the no-auditor outcome, or the plan must guarantee an audit path.

The third edge case ('files with missing vulnerability annotations... treat as unknown and exclude, or default to zero, documented in assumptions') has no corresponding plan element. Phase 2/3 tasks cover parse errors and size skips but never state the missing-annotation policy. Add an explicit handling rule to Phase 2/3 (e.g., 'missing annotations default to count 0, documented in assumptions') per the spec's own suggested option.

The plan's own Dataset Strategy states CodeVulnBench and the human-written subset (Juliet) have 'NO verified source found'. The fail-loud ingest design is honest, but as written the plan cannot produce any real results — the core data resource is unresolved. The plan should propose at least one concrete, verifiable open dataset pair (e.g., a Hugging Face LLM-code corpus with a reachable URL plus a human-code corpus) so the spec amendment it requests has a candidate, rather than deferring the entire dataset selection to execution time where the run is designed to halt.

Task 1 says ingest 'attempts programmatic download of CodeVulnBench' but no manifest source is named anywhere in the plan or research.md. The manifest-driven design needs at least a placeholder manifest schema entry (source id, expected checksum reference) so the 'canonical source' required by Constitution Principle I is defined before implementation.

concerns.location: plan.md: Constitution Check / Complexity Tracking; spec.md:FR-002; constitution.md: Principle VI
concerns.text: Plan omits SonarQube while spec FR-002 ('Bandit, Semgrep, SonarQube') and Constitution Principle VI ('configured static analysis pipeline (Bandit, Semgrep, SonarQube)') both mandate it. The plan flags this for amendment, but no amendment exists — the constitution still says 1.0.0 with SonarQube required. As written, the plan violates Principle VI and FR-002; either the constitution must be amended (version bump + Sync Impact Report per its own procedure) or the plan must include SonarQube. A flag in plan.md does not reconcile the documents.

concerns.location: plan.md: Summary 'Scope inconsistency'; spec.md:FR-001 and Assumptions
concerns.text: FR-001 mandates downloading CodeVulnBench and a human-written subset, and the spec's Assumptions state they are 'publicly available, stable, and accessible' — but research.md finds NO verified source for either. The plan correctly refuses to fabricate, but the spec and plan are now contradictory: the spec asserts availability the plan cannot deliver. The spec must be amended to name a verifiable dataset pair (or the FR relaxed) before the plan can be internally consistent.

concerns.location: data-model.md: Entities; plan.md Phase 2/3; quickstart.md Full run
concerns.text: Several artifacts named by the plan and quickstart have no entity/field definition in data-model.md: per_file_analysis.csv (in the derivation chain but no entity), per_file_density.csv, audit_sample.csv, cwe_density_by_group.csv, resource_usage.csv, and audit_metrics.csv. The derivation chain references per_file_analysis.csv yet the Entities section never defines its fields (they only exist in the contract schema). Add entity definitions or map each output to its defining contract.

concerns.location: plan.md: Constitution Check table, Principle VI row
concerns.text: Principle VI status is listed as 'PASS (with flag)' while the row text and Complexity Tracking describe a partial non-compliance pending amendment. 'PASS' contradicts the flagged violation; the status should be FAIL/FLAGGED until the amendment is ratified.

audit_sample.csv, audit_verdicts.csv, and audit_metrics.csv are produced/consumed by plan Tasks 8 and the quickstart but have no contract schema, unlike the three other derived outputs. Either add an audit contract or note in data-model.md that the AuditRecord entity definition serves as the schema.

The audit design cannot compute recall or FPR. Recall requires false negatives (true vulnerabilities the tools MISSED), and FPR = FP/(FP+TN) requires true-negative counts from clean files. The plan audits only DETECTED findings (audit_sample.csv drawn from findings.csv), which yields at most precision. As designed, SC-006/SC-007 are unmeasurable — the analysis would either report 'not_available' or silently mislabel precision as recall/FPR. The audit must be extended to sample non-flagged files/locations (or use datasets with ground-truth vulnerability annotations) for recall/FPR to be defined.

Construct validity of the comparison groups: Juliet Test Suite is a SYNTHETIC benchmark of deliberately-injected vulnerabilities (paired vulnerable/fixed cases), not representative human-written code. Using it as the 'human' group means the study compares LLM output against adversarially-constructed test cases — any density difference reflects benchmark construction, not human coding practice. The plan flags dataset availability but not this validity problem; the spec amendment it requests must also name a comparison corpus that is genuinely human-authored production code, or the research question is not answerable as posed.

The two 'independent' tests are not independent robustness checks of the same hypothesis: the NB GLM tests count differences with a log(LOC) offset (a rate model), while MW-U on per-file densities tests a distributional shift of a ratio — they can legitimately disagree. This is acceptable as a sensitivity analysis, but the plan should state which hypothesis each test addresses and pre-specify how divergence will be interpreted, rather than presenting MW-U as a 'robustness check' of the NB result.

No plan element addresses confounding by language mix between groups. If LLM and human corpora differ in language composition (Python vs Java vs JS), and Bandit/Semgrep sensitivity differs by language, the group coefficient absorbs tool-coverage differences, not vulnerability differences. The NB model should include language as a covariate (or the analysis be stratified/per-language); currently only group is a predictor.
